name: Relative Depth Loss
definition: A loss function that uses MVS depth priors to regularize geometry by comparing MVS depth against rendered depth, using thresholding to reject erroneous MVS values and weighting by rendering certainty.
summary: Relative Depth Loss is a regularization term that constrains radiance field geometry by aligning rendered median depth with depth priors, distinguishing itself through high sensitivity to close-depth errors and rejection of erroneous values via thresholding.
